description: International standard defining the format of public key certificates, specifying fields like Serial Number, Signature Algorithm, Issuer, Validity Period, and Subject.
Certificate Extension | Allows a single SSL/TLS certificate to secure multiple domain names (e.g., example.com, example.net, and sub.example.com).
Certificate that covers a base domain and all first-level subdomains using an asterisk (e.g., *.example.com covers dev.example.com and mail.example.com).
Certificate signed by the entity creating it rather than a trusted CA. Triggers browser security warnings; never use in public production.
Base64 encoded ASCII text certificate format starting with '-----BEGIN CERTIFICATE-----'. Standard for Web/Linux servers (Apache, Nginx).
Distinguished Encoding Rules | Raw binary encoded certificate format. Common in Java environments and Windows platforms.
Binary archive format used to store both the Public Certificate AND Private Key in a single password-protected file. Used in Windows/IIS.
Base64 ASCII format that contains certificates and chain certificates, but NEVER contains the private key.
